items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-15
items.q: Sounds a little bit like the Lenny Tristano school or something.

ctx.x: Could you do it again, whistle it again? I want to hold the mic around here a little closer. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. .
Just something like that. But I thought it was kind of unusual. Sounds a little bit like the Lenny Tristano school or something. It was surprising to hear in that style.
You all said something about Dizzy as he was leaving.

items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: sounds like something Lenny Tristano might have written in Conception

ctx.x: Without anybody else taking the straight melody.

No, sometimes he'd play it as an ensemble lead or sometimes he'd play it as a solo. Uh, yeah, without anybody else playing the straight melody. It would, and, uh, and then he sometimes he used that to take the thing out. In other words, he'd play that for two or three choruses in a row. And sometimes he'd, uh, he'd go to a simpler riff to take the thing out from that. Yeah. And, uh, I, I, one of the few things that I can remember musically was, uh, that had never been recorded, was the, I don't think it had been…
Did you ever hear him where you, uh, thought he was trying to play a Louis chorus or anything?
